results.summary: This project implements a BISS-C master that acquires position from an absolute encoder and produces a pulse output to synchronize an external trigger with the acquisition. It includes an SPI register interface using CPOL=1 and CPHA=1 with an 8-bit command plus 32-bit data frame, where the top command bit selects read or write. Extra features include BISS-C delay compensation and spare UIO control via registers that can be synchronized with the trigger. Testing requires a BISS-C encoder connected through an RS422 transceiver and optionally an external instrument on the pulse output.

results.summary: This project generates two sinusoidal waveforms with a fixed 90-degree phase offset (I/Q signals) using Direct Digital Synthesis. The outputs are presented as Pulse Code Modulation via two first-order sigma-delta modulators. The DDS block can be prescaled by sending a prescaler value through the SPI port. The oscillator design is based on a published recursive sinusoid generation algorithm, and recommended external hardware includes a digital buffer and two RC filters.

results.summary: This project implements a 4-bit maximum-length Linear Feedback Shift Register using the feedback polynomial x4+x+1 with taps at bit positions 3 and 0. On every rising clock edge the register shifts left by one position and a feedback bit computed as the XOR of bits 3 and 0 is inserted at the LSB. When the active-low reset is asserted the register loads the seed value 0x1, and the LFSR cycles through all 15 non-zero states before repeating. The 4-bit output appears on uo_out[3:0], the upper nibble is always zero, and no external hardware is required.

The design implements a simple security mechanism for controlling access. It is notable for its educational value in demonstrating sequential logic and state machines.
results.summary: This project implements a digital tremolo modulation controller intended for guitar pedal applications, generating a PWM signal that can be converted to a smooth analog control signal with an RC filter. At its center is an 8-bit low frequency oscillator whose rate is set by the rate select inputs, feeding a waveform generator that produces saw up, saw down, square and triangle shapes. Depth logic controls the intensity of the tremolo effect, and the resulting modulation level is compared against a PWM counter to produce the output. The design is verified with Cocotb testbenches covering reset, enable, PWM generation, rate, waveform, depth and debug outputs, and requires external RC filtering, an op-amp buffer and analog tremolo staging.

results.summary: This project implements a Secure V2X Mini Demonstrator using an 8-bit Linear Feedback Shift Register. The design accepts an 8-bit plaintext input on ui_in and internally generates an 8-bit pseudo-random key stream with the LFSR. The plaintext is XORed with the key stream to produce masked output data on uo_out, with the LFSR updating on every rising clock edge. No external hardware is required, and testing involves applying input data, clocking the design and verifying that the output changes according to the XOR operation.

results.summary_before: This design provides an on-die entropy source using a ring oscillator with NIST SP 800-90B health tests. The entropy is conditioned through ASCON-Hash256 and fed into an ASCON Hash_DRBG for key and nonce generation. A debug pin exposes raw ring-oscillator bits for post-silicon entropy characterization. It is notable for its integration of a TRNG with cryptographic conditioning.
results.summary: This project implements a configurable 8-bit PWM generator that produces a variable duty cycle signal from an 8-bit input. An internal 8-bit counter increments on every clock cycle and is compared with the duty cycle value on ui_in, driving uo_out[0] high while the counter is below the input and low otherwise. Examples include ui_in = 64 for 25% duty cycle, 128 for 50% and 192 for 75%. No external hardware is required, and testing involves applying a clock, releasing reset and observing the PWM waveform on uo_out[0].
